chats.answer:
Yes. There are robotic lawn mowers that actually collect grass clippings instead of leaving them on the lawn. They're still relatively rare, but two models stand out.

My top recommendation for 2026 is the ANTHBOT N8 robotic lawn mower, with the Mammotion YUKA robotic lawn mower + Sweeper Kit as the main alternative.

One important limitation: Automatic emptying doesn't mean the mower transfers clippings into your green waste bin. Both models dump them onto a designated area of your lawn, where you still need to collect or dispose of the pile.

The N8 also has drawbacks: it is relatively loud when collecting (around 68 dB), needs turning space, and takes longer to mow than some mulch-only robots. 
PCWorld

You can check the ANTHBOT N8 official store. The manufacturer's US homepage has recently advertised it for $1,359, discounted from $1,699. 
Smart, Wire-Free Robot Lawn Mowers

Which would I buy?

The ANTHBOT N8, provided your lawn is no larger than about 0.37 acre and has enough open space for it to maneuver. Its integrated collection system is more directly suited to your requirement than the YUKA's add-on sweeper.

One question that could change my recommendation: How big is your lawn — roughly 1,000, 3,000, 5,000, or 10,000+ square feet? And is it mostly flat or sloped?

chats.answer:
Yes, robotic lawn mowers that collect grass clippings do exist, but they're surprisingly rare. Most robot mowers use a mulching system, cutting the grass into tiny pieces and leaving them on the lawn.

If your requirement is a robot that actually picks up the clippings and empties them into a collection bin, you'll want to distinguish between true grass-collecting robots and robots that simply mulch.

The best choice depends on whether you want to collect grass after every mow, or whether you're also trying to collect leaves and other lawn debris.

Why I recommend the ANTHBOT N8

An independent October 2026 review by T3 found that it collected most clippings effectively, produced neat mowing patterns, and performed particularly well at sweeping leaves. 
T3

Unlike the YUKA, its collection mechanism is integrated into the mower rather than added as a rear sweeper.

One important limitation: automatic emptying doesn't mean the clippings disappear. The mower deposits them in a designated spot, where you still need to dispose of them.

For a lawn up to roughly one-third of an acre, the N8 would be my first choice, provided you have room for it to navigate.
